summary:
Josip Torbar (1889–1963) was a Croatian Peasant Party (HSS) politician and lawyer who served in Yugoslav governments before World War II and sought to strengthen the HSS under the Ustaše regime in the Independent State of Croatia (NDH).

A close associate of HSS leader Vladko Maček, Torbar became a member of parliament in 1935 and served as minister of posts, telegraph and telephone from 1939. After the 1941 Axis invasion, he stayed loyal to Maček. Though the Ustaše banned the HSS, Torbar met several times with leader Ante Pavelić, pressing for policy changes, the release of detained HSS members and a greater role for the party.

In 1943–44, Torbar helped plan the Lorković–Vokić plot, which aimed to remove Pavelić, disarm German forces and transfer power to the HSS with Western Allied support. The plot failed, and Torbar was imprisoned until May 1945. He fled to Italy, then Argentina and Canada, settling in New York in 1953. He died there in 1963; his remains were transferred to Zagreb in 1995.
